data.name: GuestFiles_ExecBlockedTitle
data.value: The guest agent blocks command execution

data.name: GuestFiles_UnblockLinux
data.value: Run the commands below as root inside the guest, then click [Reconnect]. RHEL, Rocky, Alma, Oracle Linux and similar block command execution by default (/etc/sysconfig/qemu-ga): with an allow list (FILTER_RPC_ARGS="--allow-rpcs=…") only the commands the file view needs (guest-exec, guest-file-*) are added; with a block list (--block-rpcs, BLACKLIST_RPC) that line is commented out. The agent is then restarted.

data.name: GuestFiles_UnblockSelinux
data.value: With SELinux the last command (virt_qemu_ga_run_unconfined) is also needed - it lets commands run by the agent read and write files.

data.name: GuestFiles_UnblockLinuxOther
data.value: If it is still blocked, check the agent arguments (systemctl cat qemu-guest-agent) and /etc/qemu/qemu-ga.conf for block-rpcs/allow-rpcs. With SELinux, setsebool -P virt_qemu_ga_run_unconfined on may also be needed.

data.name: GuestFiles_UnblockWindows
data.value: In an administrator PowerShell inside the guest, run the commands below to remove the command filter (-b/--block-rpcs, -a/--allow-rpcs) from the QEMU Guest Agent service arguments and restart the service, then click [Reconnect]. The second line shows the current arguments.

data.name: GuestFiles_UnblockScript

data.value: The file is named authorized_keys. Register the key in the target user's home; do not use sudo to run this in another user's home. Permissions are set to 700 for .ssh and 600 for authorized_keys. Keep the private key on this PC; register only the public key on the server. This command is for Linux · Unix. If the server uses a different AuthorizedKeysFile path, use that location.

data.value: For certificate authentication, send the public key for {0} to your CA to issue an OpenSSH user certificate. Configure the issued certificate and its matching private key in the account profile.

data.name: SshSetup_CertificateNote
data.value: The server must trust the issuing CA. An administrator can configure the CA public key file with TrustedUserCAKeys in sshd_config, or register the CA public key with the cert-authority option in the target user's authorized_keys. The certificate's user principal must also be allowed. Registering an ordinary user public key alone does not configure certificate authentication. A newly generated key needs a separately issued certificate.
